description: Chrome Player A's snapshot matches the separate host UI request_party_data member list and active PC; when requested, an independent Firefox Player B agrees as well.

checks.description: Chrome Player A's snapshot party members and active PC match the host Chrome context's canonical request_party_data response.
Independent Firefox Player B agrees with Chrome Player A on party and active PC.

description: A host UI user_input commit appears once and in strictly increasing sequence order in Chrome Player A and, when requested, Firefox Player B.

checks.description: The host UI commit appears once and in order in the Chrome player projection.
The same host commit appears once and in order in the independent Firefox player projection.

description: Chrome Player A validates the active-PC selection; the independent Firefox client and cross-client revision race are covered when Firefox is requested.

checks.description: Chrome Player A can select only a canonical party member and reflects the authoritative revision.
Firefox receives the canonical active-PC selection and, for a four-PC party, independent clients converge on a same-revision selection race.

description: Approved sheets, initiative/combat, and projected busy/ready state match the server snapshot in Chrome Player A and, when requested, Firefox Player B.

checks.description: Chrome Player A renders the approved sheet, combat order, and projected busy state.
Firefox Player B renders the same approved sheet, combat order, and projected busy state.

description: Submitting an identical command twice with one request ID returns the original receipt and enqueues one transcript input in Chrome, with Firefox convergence when requested.

checks.description: Chrome receives the original repeated-request receipt and observes one transcript input.
Firefox observes the single accepted transcript input from the repeated request.

description: A full one-item runtime queue returns a busy receipt without appending the rejected input; cross-client concurrency uses Firefox when requested.

checks.description: Chrome's player session can fill the queue and receives one busy result without appending the rejected input.
Independent Chrome and Firefox player sessions exercise concurrent queue admission.

description: Refresh and offline/online reconnect hydrate canonical state without resubmitting draft input in Chrome and, when requested, Firefox.

checks.description: Chrome refresh and reconnect resynchronize without replaying an unsent draft.
Firefox refresh and reconnect resynchronize without replaying an unsent draft.

description: A Chrome player page remains open during a verified tmp/combat_capture host restart; pending input becomes uncertain and a fresh snapshot resynchronizes. Firefox resynchronization is additionally covered when requested.

checks.description: Chrome retains uncertainty, does not replay input, and resynchronizes to the restarted server instance.
Firefox independently resynchronizes to the restarted server instance without replaying Chrome's pending input.

description: With only tmp/combat_capture/web/frontend/dist absent, host UI remains usable, the player listener fails closed in available browsers, and the original bundle is restored with manifest digests verified.

checks.description: The separate host Chrome context remains usable and Chrome cannot reach the failed-closed player listener.
Firefox cannot reach the failed-closed player listener.

description: With one sandbox dist asset digest corrupted, host UI remains usable, the player listener fails closed in available browsers, and the original bundle is restored with manifest digests verified.

checks.description: The separate host Chrome context remains usable and Chrome cannot reach the failed-closed player listener.
Firefox cannot reach the failed-closed player listener.

description: Host-only routes and events are refused on the player origin, with no privileged payload or host marker in the loaded JavaScript for each requested player browser.

checks.description: Chrome's player origin refuses host routes/events and its loaded JavaScript has no host-only markers.
Firefox's player origin refuses host routes/events and its loaded JavaScript has no host-only markers.
